prompt: In the JGraphT-based graph used here, what do vertices represent and what do edges represent? Two short sentences.
notes: Vertices = positions (incl. quasi-positions); edges = StagedTags (recognized concepts)

prompt: What JGraphT class is used to represent the tag graph (the exact class name)?
What graph algorithm is used to enumerate viable interpretations of the phrase, and what is the maximum number of interpretations returned by default? One sentence + one number.
Quasi-positions are introduced into the graph when handling what kind of synonym? And how are they implemented (what's special about their integer value)? Two sentences.
notes: Multi-word synonyms; quasi-positions are negative integers acting as virtual intermediate vertices

prompt: What does it mean for a path through the graph to have 'full coverage' of the phrase? One sentence.
notes: Path edges cover every token position from start to end; no gaps

prompt: Name the two main AmbiguityResolver implementations and the kind of overlap each handles. Brief.
notes: PathAmbiguityResolver (drops weaker alternatives where strong complete path exists), ShingleOverlappingAmbiguityResolver (within same field, keeps highest weighted-boost path)

prompt: How does ShingleOverlappingAmbiguityResolver compute 'weighted boost' for ranking competing tags within the same field? Express the formula.
When would I use NopAmbiguityResolver instead of one of the actual resolvers? One sentence.

must_match_regex: [Dd]ebug|[Kk]eep all|[Nn]o.?op|don'?t resolve|preserve all|fallback stage|specific stage|debugging|see raw

notes: When the stage explicitly wants to keep all interpretations, or for debugging

prompt: If both ShingleOverlappingAmbiguityResolver and PathAmbiguityResolver are configured for a stage, which order produces correct results? One sentence + brief why.
notes: ShingleOverlapping first (drops within-field redundancy), then Path (drops cross-field weaker interpretations)
